answer: Latency-triangulated wharf admission: a new identity claims one berth at a single wharf and must prove real presence there. Three independent beacons send zephyr-fast cipher nonces that the applicant must answer within tight latency bounds matching one physical location; each berth admits only one identity per epoch. A Sybil farmer cannot fake this from one server farm, because forged latency betrays distance, and each fake berth demands a real machine, real bandwidth, and a real host in another region. Mass identities thus cost mass infrastructure, not just keystrokes.
